title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: SyncroSim software platform helps turn data forecasts. core SyncroSim engine automatically structures existing data, regardless original format. SyncroSim transforms structured data forecasts running pipeline calculations (.e. suite models). Finally, SyncroSim provides rich interface interact data models, allowing explore track consequences alternative “-” forecasting scenarios. Within software framework ability use create SyncroSim packages. details consult SyncroSim online documentation.

title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: rsyncrosim R package designed facilitate development modeling workflows SyncroSim software framework. Using rsyncrosim interface, simulation models can added run SyncroSim transform scenario-based datasets model forecasts. R package takes advantage general features SyncroSim, defining scenarios spatial non-spatial inputs, running Monte Carlo simulations, summarizing model outputs. rsyncrosim requires SyncroSim 2.2.13 higher. details consult rsyncrosim CRAN documentation.

what: Create a new library using ssimLibrary()
title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: SyncroSim library file (.ssim extension) stores model inputs outputs. format SyncroSim library unique SyncroSim package associated. use ssimLibrary() function create new SsimLibrary object R connected (session) SyncroSim library file. Note: SyncroSim installed default location, need specify session argument creating loading library. However, SyncroSim installed non-default location, must include session argument creating loading library making subsequent calls library. can also use ssimLibrary() function open existing library. instance, now created library called “helloworldLibrary.ssim”, simply specify want open library using name argument. name argument takes path SyncroSim library .ssim file like open. Since “helloworldLibrary” working directory need specify full path library. Note: want create new library file existing library name rather opening existing library, can use overwrite=TRUE ssimLibrary() function.
code: # Create a new library myLibrary <- ssimLibrary(name = "helloworldLibrary.ssim",                          session = mySession,                          packages = "helloworldTime")  # Check library information myLibrary ## Package <helloworldTime v2.1.1> added ## class                      : SsimLibrary ## session [Session]          : C:\PROGRA~1\SYNCRO~1, printCmd=FALSE ## filepath [character]       : path/to/helloworldLibrary.ssim ## datasheetNames [data.frame]: scope,package,name,displayName,isSingle,displayMember # Open existing library myLibrary <- ssimLibrary(name = "helloworldLibrary.ssim")

title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: SyncroSim library contains one SyncroSim projects, represented Project object R. Projects typically store model inputs common scenarios. situations need single project library; default new library starts single project named “Definitions” (unique projectId= 1). project() function used create retrieve projects. what: Create a new scenario using scenario()
title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: Finally, SyncroSim project contains one scenarios, represented Scenario object R. Scenarios store specific inputs outputs associated transformer SyncroSim. SyncroSim models can broken one transformers. transformer essentially runs series calculations input data transform output data. Scenarios can contain multiple transformers connected series pipelines, output one transformer becomes input next. scenario can identified unique scenarioId. scenario() function used create retrieve scenarios. Note ssimObject can name library project.
code: # Create a new scenario (associated with the default project) myScenario = scenario(ssimObject = myProject, scenario = "My first scenario")  # Check scenario information myScenario ## class                      : Scenario ## projectId [numeric]        : 1 ## scenarioId [numeric]       : 1 ## parentId [numeric]         : 0 ## folderId [numeric]         : 0 ## session [Session]          : C:\PROGRA~1\SYNCRO~1, printCmd=FALSE ## filepath [character]       : path/to/helloworldLibrary.ssim ## datasheetNames [data.frame]: scope,package,name,displayName,isSingle,displayMember

title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: SyncroSim library contains multiple SyncroSim datasheets. SyncroSim datasheet simply table data stored library, represent input output data transformers. Datasheets scope: either library, project, scenario. Datasheets library scope represent data specified entire library, location backup folder. Datasheets project scope represent data shared scenarios within project. Datasheets scenario scope represent data must specified generated scenario. can view datasheets varying scopes using datasheet() function rsyncrosim. want see information datasheet, scope datasheet accepts single row data, can set optional argument TRUE. output can see Run Control Inputs datasheets accept single row data (.e. isSingle = TRUE). something consider configure model inputs. view specific datasheet rather just data frame available datasheets, set name parameter datasheet() function name datasheet want view. general syntax name : “<name package>_<name Datasheet>“. list datasheets , can see 3 datasheets specific helloworldTime package. , viewing contents SyncroSim datasheet R data frame. Although SyncroSim datasheets R data frames represented tables data predefined columns unlimited number rows, underlying structure tables differ.

what: Configure model inputs using datasheet() and addRow()
title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: Currently Inputs scenario datasheet empty! need add values Inputs datasheet (InputDatasheet) can run model. First, assign Inputs datasheet new data frame variable. Check columns need input values type values columns require (e.g. string, numeric, logical) using str() base R function. function also let us know certain columns factors specific acceptable values. Inputs datasheet requires 2 values: m : slope linear equation. b : intercept linear equation. Now, update Inputs data frame. can done many ways (e.g. using dplyr package), rsyncrosim also provides helper function called addRow() easily adding new rows R data frames. addRow() function takes targetDataframe first value (case, Inputs data frame want update), data frame new rows append input data frame second value.
code: # Assign contents of the Inputs datasheet to an R data frame myInputDataframe <- datasheet(myScenario,                               name = "helloworldTime_InputDatasheet") # Check the columns of the input data frame str(myInputDataframe) ## 'data.frame':    0 obs. of  2 variables: ##  $ m: num  ##  $ b: num # Create input data and add it to the input data frame myInputRow <- data.frame(m = 3, b = 10) myInputDataframe <- addRow(myInputDataframe, myInputRow)  # Check values myInputDataframe ##   m  b ## 1 3 10

what: Saving modifications to datasheets using saveDatasheet()
title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: Now complete data frame Inputs, save data frame respective SyncroSim datasheets using saveDatasheet() function. Since datasheet scenario-scoped, save scenario level setting ssimObject = myScenario.
code: # Save Inputs R data frame to a SyncroSim datasheet saveDatasheet(ssimObject = myScenario, data = myInputDataframe,               name = "helloworldTime_InputDatasheet") ## Datasheet <helloworldTime_InputDatasheet> saved

title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: Next, need add data Pipeline datasheet. Pipeline datasheet built-SyncroSim datasheet, meaning comes every SyncroSim library regardless packages library uses.Pipeline datasheet determines transformer stage scenarios run order. use term “transformers” constitute scripts transform input data output data. Use code assign Pipeline datasheet new data frame variable check values required datasheet. Pipeline datasheet requires 2 values: StageNameId : pipeline transformer stage. column factor single level: “Hello World Time (R)”. RunOrder : numerical order stages run. , use addRow() saveDatasheet() functions update Pipeline datasheet transformer(s) want run order want run . case, single transformer available helloworldTime package, called “Hello World Time (R)”, add transformer data frame set RunOrder 1.
code: # Assign contents of the Pipeline datasheet to an R data frame myPipeline <- datasheet(myScenario,                         name = "core_Pipeline")  # Check the columns of the Pipeline data frame str(myPipeline) ## 'data.frame':    0 obs. of  2 variables: ##  $ StageNameId: Factor w/ 1 level "Hello World Time (R)":  ##  $ RunOrder   : num # Create Pipeline data and add it to the Pipeline data frame myPipelineRow <- data.frame(StageNameId = "Hello World Time (R)", RunOrder = 1) myPipeline <- addRow(myPipeline, myPipelineRow)  # Check values myPipeline ##            StageNameId RunOrder ## 1 Hello World Time (R)        1 # Save Pipeline R data frame to a SyncroSim Datasheet saveDatasheet(ssimObject = myScenario,                data = myPipeline,               name = "core_Pipeline") ## Datasheet <core_Pipeline> saved

title: Introduction to rsyncrosim
text: one datasheet need configure package run. Run Control datasheet provides information many timesteps use model. , set minimum maximum timesteps model. ’ll add information R data frame add Run Control datasheet using addRow(). need specify data following 2 columns: MinimumTimestep : starting time point simulation. MaximumTimestep : end time point simulation.
code: # Assign contents of the run control datasheet to an R data frame runSettings <- datasheet(myScenario, name = "helloworldTime_RunControl")  # Check the columns of the run control data frame str(runSettings) ## 'data.frame':    0 obs. of  2 variables: ##  $ MinimumTimestep: num  ##  $ MaximumTimestep: num # Create run control data and add it to the run control data frame runSettingsRow <- data.frame(MinimumTimestep = 1,                              MaximumTimestep = 10) runSettings <- addRow(runSettings, runSettingsRow)  # Check values runSettings ##   MinimumTimestep MaximumTimestep ## 1               1              10 # Save run control R data frame to a SyncroSim datasheet saveDatasheet(ssimObject = myScenario, data = runSettings,               name = "helloworldTime_RunControl") ## Datasheet <helloworldTime_RunControl> saved

what: Setting the number of multiprocessing jobs
title: Introduction to rsyncrosim

Inputs datasheet First, assign contents Inputs datasheet new data frame variable using datasheet(), check columns need input values. Inputs datasheet requires three values: mMean : mean normal distribution determine slope linear equation. mSD : standard deviation normal distribution determine slope linear equation. InterceptRasterFile : file path raster image, cell image intercept linear equation. example, external file using InterceptRasterFile simple 5x5 raster TIF file generated using raster package R. file used vignette can found . Add values new data frame, use addRow() function rsyncrosim update input data frame Finally, save updated R data frame SyncroSim datasheet using saveDatasheet(). Run Control datasheet Run Control datasheet sets number iterations minimum maximum time steps model. ’ll assign contents datasheet new data frame variable well add update information data frame using addRow(). need specify data following four columns: MaximumIteration : total number iterations run model . MinimumTimestep : starting time point simulation. MaximumTimestep : end time point simulation. Note: fourth hidden column, MinimumIteration, also exists Run Control datasheet (default=1). code: # Load the Terminology datasheet to a new R data frame  terminology <- datasheet(myProject, name = "stsim_Terminology")  # Check the columns of the Terminology data frame str(terminology) ## 'data.frame':    1 obs. of  9 variables: ##  $ AmountLabel          : chr "Area" ##  $ AmountUnits          : Factor w/ 5 levels "acres","hectares",..: 1 ##  $ StateLabelX          : chr "Class" ##  $ StateLabelY          : chr "Subclass" ##  $ PrimaryStratumLabel  : chr "Primary Stratum" ##  $ SecondaryStratumLabel: chr "Secondary Stratum" ##  $ TertiaryStratumLabel : chr "Tertiary Stratum" ##  $ TimestepUnits        : chr "Timestep" ##  $ StockUnits           : chr "Tons" # Edit the values of the StateLabelX and AmountUnits columns terminology$AmountUnits <- "hectares" terminology$StateLabelX <- "Forest Type"  # Saves edits as a SyncroSim datasheet saveDatasheet(ssimObject = myProject,                data = terminology,                name = "stsim_Terminology") ## Datasheet <stsim_Stratum> saved # Create a vector containing the State Class labels  forestTypes <- c("Coniferous", "Deciduous", "Mixed")  # Add values as a data frame to a SyncroSim datasheet saveDatasheet(myProject,                data.frame(Name = forestTypes),                "stsim_StateLabelX",                force = TRUE) ## Datasheet <stsim_StateLabelX> saved # Add values as a data frame directly to an stsim datasheet saveDatasheet(myProject,                data.frame(Name = c("All")),                "stsim_StateLabelY",                force = TRUE) ## Datasheet <stsim_StateLabelY> saved # Create a new R data frame containing the names of the State Classes  # and their corresponding data stateClasses <- data.frame(Name = forestTypes) stateClasses$StateLabelXId <- stateClasses$Name stateClasses$StateLabelYId <- "All" stateClasses$Id <- c(1, 2, 3)  # Save stateClasses R data frame to a SyncroSim datasheet saveDatasheet(myProject, stateClasses, "stsim_StateClass", force = TRUE) ## Datasheet <stsim_StateClass> saved # Create an R data frame containing transition type data  transitionTypes <- data.frame(Name = c("Fire", "Harvest", "Succession"),                                Id = c(1, 2, 3))  # Save transitionTypes R data frame to a SyncroSim datasheet saveDatasheet(myProject, transitionTypes, "stsim_TransitionType", force = TRUE) ## Datasheet <stsim_TransitionType> saved # Create an R data frame containing a column of transition type names  transitionGroups <- data.frame(Name = c("Fire", "Harvest", "Succession"))  # Save transitionGroups R data frame to a SyncroSim datasheet saveDatasheet(myProject, transitionGroups, "stsim_TransitionGroup", force = T) ## Datasheet <stsim_TransitionGroup> saved # Create an R data frame that contains Transition Type Group names transitionTypesGroups <- data.frame(TransitionTypeId = transitionTypes$Name,                                     TransitionGroupId = transitionGroups$Name)  # Save transitionTypesGroups R data frame to a SyncroSim datasheet saveDatasheet(myProject,                transitionTypesGroups,                "stsim_TransitionTypeGroup",                force = T) ##
